sources.entry: syncthing-macosx - Frugal nativemacOS macOS Syncthing application bundle.

summary.one_liner: A native macOS menu-bar tray app that bundles and wraps the Syncthing daemon so it behaves like a regular Mac application instead of a command-line tool with a web interface.
summary.what_it_does: The app bundles its own Syncthing binary and runs it as a background process, managed from a tray icon that shows sync status. From the tray you can open the Syncthing WebGUI in your preferred browser, open shared folders in Finder, and optionally start it at login without configuring a system service. Logs are written to ~/Library/Application Support/Syncthing/syncthing.log. Updates are delivered through Sparkle using GitHub Releases, and the bundled Syncthing's own auto-updater is disabled. The README describes the project as deliberately lean, with no graphs or advanced configuration windows. Extra Syncthing command-line arguments can be set through macOS defaults, and the Syncthing process priority can be set to Normal, Utility, or Background.
use_cases: sync files between Mac and other devices
run Syncthing on macOS without the command line
keep a Syncthing install auto-updated on a Mac
connect a Mac to a local Syncthing instance
build a signed macOS Syncthing DMG
notable: Wraps the official Syncthing daemon in a native macOS tray app with a bundled binary
Auto-updates via Sparkle using GitHub Releases, with its own update mechanism
Settings stored in NSUserDefaults and editable from the terminal with defaults write
Can point to a custom Syncthing executable outside the app bundle for power users
Available as a DMG or via Homebrew cask (syncthing-app)
caveats: Syncthing v1 is deprecated and no longer receives updates; v2 needs at least macOS 12
Only manages a local Syncthing instance; remote instances are not supported
Another Syncthing instance or wrapper running at the same time will break this app
Auto-update must be manually disabled on unsupported macOS versions
